annotation_description: MiMo Worrier skipped their land drop on turn 2 with three lands in hand. Missing a land drop this early is a significant tempo loss, especially when they have a 3-drop (Formidable Speaker) they'd want to cast on turn 3. Playing a land costs nothing and is pure upside.

They have Gloomlake Verge, Island, Island, Swamp in hand but haven't played their land for the turn yet. Even if they play a land after this resolves, they'll be down to 1 land on board. This is a catastrophic tempo loss on turn 2 - they're destroying one of the opponent's dual lands (which the opponent can replace with a basic) while setting themselves back enormously on mana development. They have Deadly Cover-Up (5 mana) and Stock Up (3 mana) in hand that they need to cast, and this play delays them by multiple turns. The opponent also gets to search for a basic land, so it's not even denying them a color permanently.

annotation_description: Activating Demolition Field's destroy ability on turn 3 costs 2 mana + tap + sacrifice, leaving GPT4om Gramps with only Watery Grave (1 land) after this resolves. The opponent gets to search for a basic land, so they net a land while GPT4om Gramps searches for one basic but sacrificed one, effectively trading down. More critically, GPT4om Gramps has only 2 lands in play and needs to develop mana to cast Deadly Cover-Up (5 mana) and Stock Up (3 mana). Sacrificing Demolition Field on turn 3 when the opponent has no threatening board presence (just lands, no creatures) sets back mana development significantly. The opponent's lands (Watery Grave, Breeding Pool, Willowrush Verge) aren't providing any unique strategic advantage worth destroying at the cost of falling behind on mana. Additionally, both players search for basics, so the opponent replaces their destroyed land.

GPT4om Gramps cast Stock Up before playing a land. They have Gloomlake Verge, Island, Undercity Sewers, and Swamp in hand. They should play a land first (likely Undercity Sewers for the surveil trigger before drawing, or Gloomlake Verge to have 4 mana available). By casting Stock Up first with only 3 lands, they use all their mana and miss the opportunity to surveil before the draw spell (if playing Undercity Sewers) or to have mana available after resolving Stock Up. Playing land before spells is fundamental sequencing.

annotation_description: Activating Demolition Field before playing a land for the turn. With Gloomlake Verge, Island, Swamp, and Undercity Sewers in hand, playing a land first would leave mana available after the activation to hold up Essence Scatter (1U) or Requiting Hex (B). Additionally, using Demolition Field on Turn 4 to destroy an opponent's land when the opponent only has a 2/4 creature and the priority should be developing mana for Deadly Cover-Up or holding up countermagic is questionable.

Playing Swamp instead of Gloomlake Verge is slightly suboptimal. Gloomlake Verge produces both U and B (since they already control an Island via Watery Grave and a Swamp), so it's strictly better than a basic Swamp here - it provides the same black mana plus blue mana flexibility. Additionally, keeping basic lands in hand is better for future Demolition Field activations or in case the opponent has land destruction that cares about nonbasics. However, Gloomlake Verge entering untapped and producing both colors is more valuable than a basic Swamp right now, especially with Essence Scatter in hand wanting UU availability. With Swamp played, they have access to 1U + 2B, but with Gloomlake Verge they'd have access to 2U + 1B (or 1U + 2B), giving more flexibility for Essence Scatter.

The opponent replaces it with a basic that still enables their UB mana. Willowrush Verge is the only green mana source on board, and destroying it would likely cut the opponent off green entirely since the replacement basic land wouldn't produce green.

Playing Island instead of Gloomlake Verge reduces mana flexibility. Gloomlake Verge enters untapped and can produce either U or B (since they control both Islands and Swamps), which is strictly better than an Island that only produces U. With Deadly Cover-Up ({3}{B}{B}), Essence Scatter ({1}{U}), and Requiting Hex ({B}) in hand, having access to additional black sources matters.
